newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras says EU may curb wheat exports next week.
newsitem.headline: Legras says EU may curb wheat exports next week.

text.p: Guy Legras, the European Commission's director general for agriculture, said on Friday the European Union may scale back the tonnages of soft wheat it awards through its weekly grain auction next week.
"Next week we may give less. We may turn the screw on exports," Legras told Reuters at a farm conference organised by the AGRA farm weekly magazine.
On Thursday the European Union awarded 477,700 tonnes of free market soft wheat at its weekly grain auction.
Legras explained that the EU had exported around one million tonnes of wheat during the last two weeks.
Commenting on last Thursday's wheat award, Legras said, "We already exported a lot, we gave reasonable volumes. There was no need to give too substantial tonnages. These are reasonable tonnages."
Faced with strong demand from a flurry of world importers, excited grain traders bid last Thursday to export more than 1.3 million tonnes of EU soft wheat.
Legras linked last week's massive bid to the fact that a few traders may have tried to get hold of all the wheat export licences that were available.
"When you look at the tonnages offered you could see there were a few wise guys that were trying to play games," Legras said.
Grain exporters said earlier on Friday they needed to secure substantial wheat export licences to cover a surge of import demand from Arab nations ahead of the Ramadan Moslem fasting month.
Legras added that exporters could always exchange export certificates between themselves.
